cards.text: Welcome to Sparkle's station, friend, where every word comes straight from the heart. In this love song, a woman is speaking, and she says, "I sleep, but my heart is awake." Then, out of nowhere, a sound.

cards.question: In the night, someone is making a sound at the woman's door. Who is it?

cards.text: He calls her "my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one." Four sweet names in one breath, friend, and I gave each of my six little ones exactly ONE.

cards.question: Her beloved is outside her door in the night, his head drenched with dew. He asks her to ___ to him.

cards.text: But she's already taken off her robe and washed her feet. Friend, it's a law of the universe: the SECOND you get comfy for the night, that's when somebody knocks.

cards.question: Her robe is off, her feet are washed, and her beloved is knocking. What does the woman wonder?

answers.text: If she must put her robe back on
Why he came so late tonight
Whether the door is even locked

cards.text: Then her beloved puts his hand to the latch.

cards.question: When her beloved put his hand to the latch, her ___ pounded for him.
True or false: After wondering about her robe, the woman stays in bed and never opens the door.

cards.text: She gets up to open for him, and her fingers drip with flowing myrrh on the handles of the bolt. Friend, the only thing my bakery door ever drips with is cookie dough.

cards.question: She opens the door for her beloved, but he had ___ and ___.

cards.text: Her heart sank at his departure. It's like sprinting to the door just in time to watch the delivery truck turn the corner.

cards.question: True or false: When the woman goes looking for her beloved and calls out for him, he answers her.

cards.text: Out in the city, she runs into the watchmen making their rounds, the guardians of the walls.

cards.question: True or false: The watchmen on their rounds help the woman look for her beloved.

cards.text: Instead, they beat her and bruised her, and they took away her cloak.
Bruised and without her cloak, she turns to the daughters of Jerusalem, a group of women in this song. She solemnly charges them with one request.

cards.question: If the daughters of Jerusalem find her beloved, what does the woman want them to tell him?

answers.text: That she is sick with love
That she is tired of waiting

cards.text: The daughters of Jerusalem call her "most beautiful among women" and ask how her beloved is better than others. Basically: "Okay, what's SO special about this one?"

cards.question: True or false: The daughters of Jerusalem ask about her beloved because she charged them to give him her message.
The daughters of Jerusalem want to know what makes her beloved better than others. How does the woman answer?

answers.text: She paints a picture of what he's like
She says they'll know him when they see him
She tells them to go ask the watchmen

cards.text: And she does NOT hold back. Her beloved is dazzling and ruddy, "outstanding among ten thousand."

cards.question: The woman calls her beloved outstanding among ten thousand. What is she saying about him?

answers.text: He stands out above everyone else
He leads an army of thousands
He is famous across the land

cards.text: His head is purest gold, his hair is black as a raven, and his eyes are like doves beside the streams of water. Doves AGAIN, friend: this song has more doves than a park bench.
His cheeks are like beds of spice, and his lips are like lilies, dripping with flowing myrrh. Hold on, friend, flowing myrrh again?

cards.question: Flowing myrrh drips from her beloved's lips in her description. Where else in this passage did flowing myrrh show up?

answers.text: On her fingers at the bolt
On the cloak the watchmen took

cards.text: His arms are rods of gold, and his legs are pillars of marble set on bases of pure gold. Friend, I have been standing on a gold base this WHOLE time, and nobody ever wrote me a song.

cards.question: True or false: In her description of her beloved, the woman starts with his head and works her way down to his legs.

cards.text: Then she wraps it up: "His mouth is most sweet; he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem."

cards.question: The woman calls him "my beloved" and also "my friend." What is she saying about him?

answers.text: He is her companion as well as her love
He is only a friend to her from now on
He is a friend to the daughters as well

cards.text: Now the daughters ask, "Where has your beloved gone, O most beautiful among women? Which way has he turned?"

cards.question: After hearing her describe her beloved, the daughters of Jerusalem say they will ___ him with her.
Earlier, the woman sought her beloved but did not find him. Now she says he has gone down to his ___.

cards.text: She says he's gone to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens and to gather lilies. Picture her out there searching the city, friend, and he's picking lilies.

cards.question: True or false: After that empty doorway, the woman says she and her beloved belong to each other.

cards.text: Her beloved pastures his flock among the lilies. She opened the door to an empty night, friend, and I think she still lands right here, sure of who she belongs to.

findings.problem: The earlier cards say that the woman rises to open the door, but they provide no way to infer that her beloved had "turned" and "gone" rather than waited or stayed. Even if his departure is treated as a discovery moment, the two blanks ask for unseen wording that cannot be reasoned out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards points to a garden rather than a house or a tower. The baker can only guess the unseen location word, so this blank does not test a meaning they can reason out.
